answer: In an agent economy, every identity that wants to trade must first stake an opal bond — a deposit that is locked for the full trading season and slashed if the agent is caught faking deliveries. A falcon-style audit swarm samples transactions at random, comparing signed delivery receipts against the public ledger, so a single operator spinning up a zephyr of cheap fake identities must fund a separate bond for each one and risks losing all of them at once. Forgery stops being free and starts being ruinously expensive.
